Podduturi Subbamma vs Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport
...

on 13 September, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No. 975 of 2012
Judgment:
The appellant is petitioner and the respondent is respondent in M.V.O.P.No.938 of 2007 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Guntur.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Guntur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant filed the appeal questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal.
2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim petition.

3. The claim petitioner filed the claim petition under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act') against the respondent praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.1,70,000/- towards compensation for the death of her son by name Podduturi Durga Rao in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 13.04.1994.

4. The brief averments of the claim petition are as follows:
VGKR,J On 13.04.1994 at 7.50 a.m. when the deceased was crossing a road near Goppaludi center of Vijayawada, a bus bearing registration No.AP 9Z 4635 of the respondent being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at high speed came and hit the deceased resulting in the instantaneous death of the deceased.
The police, I Town P.S., Vijayawada, filed a charge sheet against the driver of the offending bus.
The respondent being owner of the offending bus is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

5. The respondent/APSRTC filed a written statement by denying the manner of accident, age,
avocation and income of the deceased.

It is pleaded that the deceased died due to his own negligence and the claim of the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
6.

Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues for trial:
1. Whether the deceased died in the accident caused due to rash and negligent driving of the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP 9Z 4635 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what would be the just amount of VGKR,J compensation that the petitioner would be entitled to and against whom?

sentences.text: To what relief?
7. During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioner, P.W.1 was examined and Exs.A.1 to A.5 were marked.
On behalf of the respondent/APSRTC, R.W.1 was examined and Exs.B.1 to B.6 were marked.
8. At the culmination of the enquiry, after considering the evidence on record, the Tribunal dismissed the claim petition.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the petitioner preferred the instant appeal.

9. Heard learned counsels for both the parties and perused the record.
10.

Now, the points for determination are:
1) Whether the order passed by the Tribunal needs any interference? and 2) Whether the appellant/petitioner is entitled to any compensation as prayed for?
VGKR,J 11. POINT Nos.1 & 2:

The claim petition filed by the petitioner was dismissed by the Tribunal on the ground that the respondent/APSRTC paid an amount of Rs.30,000/- to the petitioner towards full and final settlement of her claim, therefore, the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation from the respondent.
12. Since the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial and welfare legislation, it is the duty of the Tribunal to award just and fair compensation to the victims.
No doubt, the claim petition is filed under Section 163-A of the Act whereunder the petitioner need not prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the vehicle.
It is sufficient to prove that the vehicle was involved in the accident.

13. It is the case of the petitioner that on 13.04.1994 at 7.50 a.m. when the deceased was crossing a road near Goppaludi center of Vijayawada, a bus bearing registration No.AP 9Z 4635 of the respondent being driven by its driver in a rash and VGKR,J negligent manner at high speed came and hit the deceased resulting in the instantaneous death of the deceased.
14. In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus, the petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1.
She reiterated the contents of the claim petition in her chief examination affidavit.

The petitioner also relied on Exs.A.1- certified copy of first information report, Ex.A.2-certified copy of charge sheet, Ex.A.3-certified copy of inquest report and Ex.A.4- certified copy of post mortem report.
Though the respondent examined its Officer as R.W.1, but his evidence cannot be relied upon, because he is not an eye witness to the accident.
Further, the respondent did not choose to examine the driver of the offending bus who is the best person to speak about the manner of accident.

The evidence of P.W.1 coupled with Exs.A.1 to A.4 clearly prove that the petitioner established that the death of the deceased caused only on account of the accident Podduturi Subbamma vs Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport ... on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168747889/
2 in which the offending bus was involved.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal, on appreciating the material evidence on record, also came to the same conclusion.
VGKR,J
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.
15. Coming to the compensation, according to the petitioner, the deceased was aged about 21 years at the time of accident and he used to earn Rs.100/- per day by working as a labourer.
The accident occurred in the year 1994.

In those days, an ordinary coolie can easily earn Rs.50/- per day i.e.,
Rs.1,500/- p.m. and Rs.18,000/- per annum.
The claim petition is filed under Section 163-A of the Act.
So, 1/3rd from out of the annual income has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.
Having deducted as such, the annual contribution to the family members of the deceased is arrived at Rs.12,000/- (Rs.18,000/- - Rs.6,000/-).
As stated supra, the deceased was aged about 21 years as on the date of accident.
As per II Schedule to Section 163-A of the Act, the relevant multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased is "17" and the loss of dependency is arrived at Rs.2,04,000/- (Rs.12,000/- x 17).
Apart from that, an amount of Rs.1,500/- is awarded towards loss of estate and Rs.1,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses of the deceased.
VGKR,J
In total, the petitioner is entitled to a compensation of Rs.2,07,000/-.

16. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the respondent/APSRTC that the respondent had paid a lumpsum amount of Rs.30,000/- to the petitioner, who is the mother of the deceased,
towards full and final settlement of her claim for the death of the deceased, and he relied on Exs.B.1 to B.6.

17. Per contra, learned counsel for the appellant/petitioner would submit that taking advantage of the illiteracy of the petitioner and her rural background, the officials of the respondent obtained Exs.B.1 to B.6 from the petitioner to deny the just compensation.

18. On considering the material on record, this Court is of the view that the respondent cannot plead that they are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner on the sole ground that they paid an amount of Rs.30,000/- for the death of the deceased in a road accident which was caused by their driver.

Therefore, the amount of Rs.30,000/-, which was paid by the respondent to VGKR,J the petitioner, has to be deducted from out of the total compensation of Rs.2,07,000/- awarded to the petitioner, as such, the respondent is liable to pay the remaining compensation of Rs.1,77,000/-
to the petitioner, but, the petitioner claimed an amount of Rs.1,70,000/- only.

Therefore, the claim of the petitioner is restricted to Rs.1,70,000/-.
19.

In the result, the appeal is allowed and the order and decree dated 31.07.2008 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Guntur, in M.V.O.P.No.938 of 2007 are hereby set aside.

entities.label: COURT

Consequently, M.V.O.P.No.938 of 2007 is allowed granting a total compensation of Rs.1,70,000/- to the petitioner with costs and interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of payment.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount of Rs.1,70,000/- with costs and interest before the Tribunal within two months from the date of this judgment.
